overview -> physical prior and search-method handoff

global_organization_chain: The summary states the missing-aircraft decision, prior distribution, four search patterns, Bayesian update, scenario variation, and rectangle recommendation.
The contents makes the route from flight assumptions through probability theory, paths, comparisons, final remarks, and airline letter explicit.
The introduction uses two missing-aircraft incidents to frame time, cost, and survivor-recovery stakes before announcing generic search models.
The nomenclature binds grid, aircraft, detection, path, probability, and effectiveness symbols before equations use them.
The source fixes unpowered flight, one instantaneous turn, no wind/current, floating debris, flat water, runway position, and daylight limits.
Flight geometry and independent descent-angle and bearing distributions construct the initial crash-location probability field.
Bayes theorem updates searched and unsearched grid locations, derives a random-search detection probability, and defines cumulative success.
The continuous probability field becomes a one-square-mile probability grid with explicit range, runway, and daily-search inputs.
Each candidate center is evaluated by usable range, feasible search dimensions, and traversed-grid probability before posterior updating.
A parallel sweep derives square side and path length, then shows five-day posterior maps and twenty-day success curves.
The rectangle generalizes the square area relation and enumerates integer dimensions to improve coverage at greater computational cost.
Spiral geometry derives length-to-side conversion and compares its efficient but less spatially effective route with parallel sweep.
Sector geometry maps path length to an octagon but uses a local center heuristic that the source explicitly calls rudimentary.
Single/multiple aircraft, stall prior, range, mixed paths, and effectiveness variations compare cumulative success under changed scenarios.
The source distinguishes customizability and global square/rectangle optimization from computational cost, sector weakness, assumptions, and absent cost effectiveness.
Future work adds multi-plane pattern optimization, empirical parameters, cost limits, debris dynamics, weather, currents, staging, and refueling.
The conclusion reconnects flight failure, priors, Bayesian updating, paths, scenario tests, and the parallel-sweep recommendation.
References identify incident, flight, search, Bayesian, aircraft, and path sources while leaving frozen data and executable runs absent.
A fictional company letter translates the map, dynamic update, familiar paths, coordinates, and resource claims to commercial-airline readers.
Only after positive language, organization, model, result, and visual chains are complete does the final pass record formula, heuristic, calibration, and deployment warnings.

main_argument_chains.claim: A search starts with a physical trajectory prior rather than one guessed location.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Calibrate the prior to the incident before treating it as a search map.

main_argument_chains.claim: An unsuccessful search changes both searched and unsearched probabilities before the next daily path is selected.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Update the full grid rather than deleting searched cells from consideration.

main_argument_chains.claim: Path recommendation follows geometry, usable range, posterior mass, and repeated simulation rather than shape alone.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Select a path conditional on resources, runtime, and the modeled posterior.

main_argument_chains.claim: Scenario comparisons make aircraft range, failure prior, path combinations, and effectiveness explicit modifiers of the recommendation.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Use each curve only with its stated scenario inputs and unmodeled constraints.

main_argument_chains.claim: A stakeholder letter closes the loop by stating required aircraft data, dynamic updates, path outputs, and operational use.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Communicate model use while disclosing the deployment assumptions that still require operational validation.

warnings.warning: Coordinate transform parentheses and dimensions require reconstruction before numerical reuse.
The printed recurrence visibly omits h from the final fraction.
The displayed difference-quotient limit visibly tends to infinity rather than zero.
The regional criterion mixes q(z*) with a maximized area integral and needs a typed domain/objective derivation.
The printed spiral-length simplification is algebraically unusual and should be checked before inversion.
The spiral-side inverse requires an independent domain and discriminant check.
The effectiveness parameter is hypothetical and uncalibrated, so its numeric use cannot establish real detection probability.

visualization_dispositions.analytical_purpose: Glide angle theta defines the vertical trajectory input.
Bearing change phi defines the horizontal trajectory input.
Geometry supports the maximum unpowered glide-range relation.
Initial Cartesian probability density shows crash and glide modes.
Lateral range W defines search-track geometry.
Increment h illustrates incremental swept area.
Prior and posterior curves show a searched middle region.
Contour map turns the prior into a discrete search grid.
Parallel sweep makes square-path passes and lateral coverage visible.
Five-day posterior shows the square search's selected regions.
Twenty-day cumulative and daily success show square-path output.
Rectangle posterior map visualizes reduced gaps.
Rectangle success curve exposes performance and runtime tradeoff.
Spiral sweep defines the alternative path geometry.
Spiral symmetry motivates the path-length derivation.
Spiral posterior displays the selected five-day regions.
Spiral cumulative/daily curve supports path comparison.
Sector search shows the octagonal sweep geometry.
Sector parameters expose side, angle, and repeated-center structure.
Sector posterior shows the local-center heuristic outcome.
Sector cumulative/daily curve reveals lower performance.
Single-plane comparison places four path curves on one scale.
